statement.p: Water in a cylinder of height 12 ft and radius 3 ft is to be pumped out. The density of water is 62.4 lb/ft{}^3. Find the work required if
(a) The tank is full of water and the water is to be pumped over the top of the tank.
(b) The tank is full of water and the water must be pumped to a height 6 ft above the top of the tank.
(c) The depth of water in the tank is 7 ft and the water must be pumped over the top of the tank.

static.solution:
(a) We slice the water horizontally. Each slice is a cylindrical slab of radius and thickness \Delta h, so
\hbox{Volume of each slab }\approx \pi 3^2 \Delta h\hbox{ ft}^3. The density of water is \delta = 62.4 lb/ft{}^3, so \hbox{Weight of slab }\approx \delta\pi3^2 \Delta h \hbox{ lb.} Water at a height of h ft must be lifted a distance of 12 - h ft. \hbox{ Work to move one slice} =\delta \cdot \hbox{Volume} \cdot \hbox{Distance lifted} \approx \delta (\pi (3)^2 \Delta h)(12 - h)\hbox{ ft-lb.} Plugging in \delta=62.4 and since h varies from h = 0 to h = 12, the total work, W, is: W = \int_0^{12}{\delta(\pi 3^2 )(12-h)dh} = 3^2\delta \pi \int_0^{12}{(12 - h)dh} = (3^2) 62.4 \pi\left(12 h-\frac{h^2}2\right) \Bigg|_0^{12} = 127031\ {\rm lbf}. The total work required is 127031\ {\rm lbf}.
(b) This is the same as part (a) except the water must be lifted a distance of 18 - h ft. The total work is: W = \int_0^{12}{\delta(\pi 3^2 )(6-h)dh} = 3^2\delta \pi \int_0^{12}{(18 - h)dh} = (3^2) 62.4 \pi \left(18 h-\frac{h^2}2\right)\Bigg|_0^{12} = 254062\ {\rm lbf}. The total work required is 254062\ {\rm lbf}.
(c) This is the same as part (a) except that h varies from h=0 to h=7. The total work is: W = \int_0^{7}{\delta(\pi 3^2 )(12-h)dh} = 3^2\delta \pi \int_0^{7}{(12 -h)dh} = (3^2) 62.4 \pi \left(12 h-\frac{h^2}2\right)\Bigg|_0^{12} = 104977\ {\rm lbf}. The total work required is 104977\ {\rm lbf}.
